_: Hand-authored couplings per configurator design spec §4. NOT generated. rules.js is a pure interpreter for this file: facts in -> {set, show, suggest, notes, lines, order} out. Rules apply in array order; a later `set` of the same key wins.

_facts.band_translucent: true | false — the band's own translucency checkbox, state.band.translucent
_facts.tray_translucent: true | false — the tray's own translucency checkbox, state.tray.translucent
_facts.translucent_case: true when the band or the tray is translucent, i.e. when you can see the board
_facts.plate_make: fr4 | printed — the procurement fork, design spec §2 'Plate'
_facts.caps_on: true | false — state.view.caps, the one Show toggle that is also a config axis

_not_facts: state.view.* (switches / knob / stick / stabilizer / encoder / joystick) and the whole state.lighting block are RENDER ONLY. They must never become facts: the owner asked for view toggles, not more ways to change what you order. Neither may translucency on the plate, keycaps, switches or toppers: only the two CASE parts decide whether the board is on show.
_colour_is_not_a_kind: Colour and translucency are independent axes (see finishes.json _palette). Nothing here may test a finish id or a finish 'kind' — the board-mask reveal and the LED band hint both key off the translucency CHECKBOX.

rules._: Design spec §2: LED band on hints at a see-through band. The hint now lands on the band's translucency checkbox, and only while it is off — so the default build, which ships a translucent band, shows no hint at all.

notes.text: Printed plate has no copper — touch behaves like the blank variant.
Print the gauge, keep the rung that holds.
Band pocket is deliberately tight — light sand if needed.
Riser in TPU = grip base, rigid = stand.
